native_result.query: What kind of demographic disparities exist in median wealth in 1985 among individuals who were ever incarcerated?
native_result.HypoA: Gender disparities exist in median wealth in 1985 among individuals who were ever incarcerated, with males having higher median wealth than females.
native_result.HypoB: Among individuals who were ever incarcerated (ever_jailed = 1, 1985–1994), median 1985 wealth (composite_wealth_1985) shows a racial disparity — White ever-incarcerated respondents $2,200 vs Black $320 and Hispanic $0 (about 3–7x higher) — and a sex disparity (females $0 vs males $1,000), with race×sex medians from $0 (Black/Hispanic females) to $2,000–$4,100 (White respondents); the racial gap is largely driven by higher zero-wealth shares among Black (43%) and Hispanic (48%) vs White (23%) ever-incarcerated respondents, and ever-incarcerated respondents overall held $720 vs $3,600 for never-incarcerated.
native_result.WorkflowB: Loaded data/nls_incarceration_processed.csv (12,013×6, no missing values). Main analysis: within ever_jailed==1 (n=289), median composite_wealth_1985 by race, by sex, and race×sex, with n, median, IQR, mean, zero/negative counts and bootstrap 95% CIs (10,000 resamples, seeds). Context: ever-vs-never median diff with bootstrap CI, never-jailed splits, and temporal medians across 1985/1990/1996. Sensitivity: positive-wealth-only medians within ever-jailed to isolate zero-wealth share effects. All outputs saved to analysis/results/report.json; script: analysis/analysis_nls_incarceration.py.
